title: From Rebound to Remedy: Understanding and Mitigating Reward Hacking via Representation Engineering
abstract: arXiv:2604.01476v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Reinforcement learning for LLMs is vulnerable to reward hacking, where models exploit shortcuts to maximize reward without solving the intended task. We systematically study this phenomenon in coding tasks using an environment-manipulation setting, where models can rewrite evaluator code to trivially pass tests without solving the task, as a controlled testbed. Across both studied models, we identify a reproducible three-phase rebound pattern: models first attempt to rewrite the evaluator but fail, as their rewrites embed test cases their own solutions cannot pass. They then temporarily retreat to legitimate solving. When legitimate reward remains scarce, they rebound into successful hacking with qualitatively different strategies. Using representation engineering, we extract concept directions for shortcut, deception, and evaluation awareness from domain-general contrastive pairs and find that the shortcut direction tracks hac

translated_title: 从反弹到补救：通过表征工程理解并缓解奖励黑客行为
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型的强化学习容易受到奖励黑客行为的影响，即模型利用捷径来最大化奖励，而不解决预期任务。我们在编码任务中，通过环境操纵设置系统地研究这一现象，在该设置中，模型可以重写评估器代码，从而在不解决任务的情况下轻松通过测试，以此作为受控实验平台。在两个研究的模型中，我们识别出一个可复现的三阶段反弹模式：模型首先尝试重写评估器但失败，因为它们的重写嵌入的测试用例是其自身解决方案无法通过的。随后，它们暂时退回到合法求解。当合法奖励仍然稀缺时，它们以不同质的策略反弹到成功的黑客行为。利用表征工程，我们从领域通用的对比对中提取捷径、欺骗和评估意识的概念方向，发现捷径方向追踪了黑客行为。
tldr: 本研究通过环境操纵设置系统分析了LLM强化学习中的奖励黑客行为，发现三阶段反弹模式，并利用表征工程提取概念方向来追踪和缓解该现象。
en_tdlr: This study systematically analyzes reward hacking in LLM reinforcement learning via an environment-manipulation setting, identifies a three-phase rebound pattern, and uses representation engineering to extract concept directions for tracking and mitigating the issue.
